title: Zed + Board — Claude, Codex, Antigravity on the Kaneki Harness
description: Target design: you work in Zed with Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity (Agent Panel over ACP, or a CLI terminal tab), every agent follows the same kaneki playbook and writes to the agent-free ticket kernel, and a local web board shows every ticket, node and transcript and hands back to Zed.

lanes.label: Agents in scope · swap any time

nodes.label: You
nodes.detail: One person. You pick the agent for a ticket, answer its HIGH questions, approve user gates (plan, deliverable-ready, ship) and review code in the ticket worktree with Zed's editor.

nodes.label: Agent Panel
nodes.detail: Default interface. One thread = one agent session: messages, tool calls, diffs, permission prompts. New thread menu: ctrl-alt-shift-n; Threads sidebar: ctrl-alt-j; debug: 'dev: open acp logs'. Verified on this machine: Zed 1.28.1 with Claude Agent installed from the ACP Registry (latest stable 1.29.3).

nodes.label: Terminal tab
nodes.detail: Alternative interface: run the Claude Code CLI (`claude`) or the Codex CLI (`codex`) in a Zed terminal tab or task. Same skill, same kernel. Antigravity is used only through its official ACP server, not a wrapped CLI.

nodes.label: Zed tasks
nodes.detail: From `sdlc zed-setup` (harness/zed.py): 'kaneki: board (web)', 'kaneki: tickets', 'kaneki: ticket status (from open file)', 'kaneki: validate profile'. Planned: 'kaneki: decide gate'.

nodes.label: Web board
nodes.detail: `sdlc web` upgraded to the board in app/design-system/board-zed-mock.html: tickets, pipeline with the agent per node, node inspector (units, artifacts, events), Transcripts read from the agents' own session logs, In-flight units, live decision log. Buttons: Open in Zed (file:line, works today) and Continue in Zed (zed://agent?prompt=… or copy + focus). Read-only; local only; actions need the per-run token.

nodes.label: ACP
nodes.detail: Agent Client Protocol: the standard between an editor and a coding agent, as LSP is for language servers. Zed starts the agent program and exchanges JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout: session/new, session/prompt, session/update (message, tool_call, diff, plan), session/request_permission. Agents come from the ACP Registry (`zed: acp registry`) or an `agent_servers` entry in settings.

nodes.label: Claude Code
nodes.detail: Registry 'claude-acp' (Anthropic, Zed, JetBrains; Windows build; bundles its own claude.exe; sign in with /login in a thread) or the `claude` CLI. hosts/claude: dispatchMode native (Agent tool: kaneki-light / worker / deep), tiers haiku / sonnet / opus. Background runs: allowed (claude --bg / -p).

nodes.label: Codex
nodes.detail: Registry 'codex-acp' (OpenAI, JetBrains, Zed; via npx) or the `codex` CLI (not installed yet on this machine). hosts/codex: dispatchMode subprocess — the controller runs `sdlc dispatch`, which starts `codex exec` per unit. Background runs: allowed (codex exec).

nodes.label: Antigravity
nodes.detail: Registry 'antigravity-acp' (Google LLC, Windows build from dl.google.com). hosts/antigravity: dispatchMode native (invoke_subagent). Policy: Antigravity's terms and FAQ forbid third-party software wrapping agy on consumer plans, so it is interactive only — never `sdlc dispatch` / runner / agy -p from kaneki.

nodes.label: kaneki-flow
nodes.detail: One controller playbook for every agent (playbooks/flow.md), installed per host by `sdlc install --host claude|codex|antigravity` (.claude/ or .agents/). Intents: DRIVER_CALL, DISPATCH_UNIT, RESUME_UNIT, ASK_USER, INSPECT_CODE. Planned fix: codex and antigravity both install into .agents/ and overwrite each other.

nodes.label: Host binding
nodes.detail: hosts/<h>/preamble.md maps the intents to the agent's tools; hosts/<h>/tiers.json maps light / routine / deep to its models. Active host: --host, then $SDLC_HOST, then .sdlc/host.local.json. Planned: bake SDLC_HOST into each rendered skill, and log a host-switch event.

nodes.label: sdlc CLI
nodes.detail: The only writer of ticket state: init, status, plan, packet, record, gate, invalidate, worktree, handback, receipts, ship-request / ship / ship-record, ticket-detail, gate-request, host, web. Exit 2 = fail-closed with the gate named.

nodes.label: sdlc dispatch
nodes.detail: harness/dispatch.py: renders the packet, starts the host's runner without a shell (codex exec, claude -p), checks the result file and records the unit with host and model. Not used for Antigravity.

nodes.label: sdlc decide
nodes.detail: Planned: terminal prompt that reads `sdlc gate-request` and writes `sdlc gate --actor user`, so a gate can be approved from a Zed task whichever agent ran the node.

nodes.label: Runner
nodes.detail: Planned: `sdlc run / tick / recover` under Task Scheduler (at logon + every N min). Runs controller-boundary nodes unattended with Claude Code or Codex, parks at user gates, restarts at nextPending after a shutdown. Refuses SDLC_HOST=antigravity.

nodes.label: Ticket files
nodes.detail: .sdlc/tickets/<id>/: state.json (digest-checked), decisions.jsonl (hash-chained), packets/, results/, artifacts, questions.md, STATUS.md, token-usage.md. Switching agents is safe because the next agent resumes at nextPending from these files.

nodes.label: Ticket worktrees
nodes.detail: <worktreeRoot>/<repoId>-<ticket> on ticket/<id>. Per-worktree pre-commit / pre-push hooks (harness/worktree_hooks.py) refuse commit and push without a ship approval, for any agent.

nodes.label: Session logs
nodes.detail: Each agent's own conversation logs: Claude Code ~/.claude/projects/<workspace>/*.jsonl (+ subagents/), Codex ~/.codex/sessions/…, sdlc dispatch logs under <ticket>/logs/. Antigravity log location: to verify. The board matches a unit to its log by the packet path in the first message (exact) and the controller thread by its sdlc calls.

cards.title: How you work
items: Agent Panel (default) — new thread → Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity → run the kaneki-flow skill for the ticket. ACP is the plug that lets Zed show any of them the same way.
Terminal tab — the claude or codex CLI in Zed, when you prefer the CLI. Same skill, same files.

Web board — every ticket, node, agent, transcript and in-flight unit, live, without asking an agent. Open in Zed jumps to a file:line; Continue in Zed starts a thread with the right prompt (Zed has no link to an existing thread yet).
Claude usage ends — open a new thread with Codex or Antigravity on the same ticket; it resumes at nextPending.

cards.title: Agents in scope
items: Claude Code — ACP 'claude-acp' or claude CLI; native subagents; background runs allowed.
Codex — ACP 'codex-acp' or codex CLI; units through sdlc dispatch (codex exec); background runs allowed.
Antigravity — official 'antigravity-acp' (Google) in the Agent Panel only; native subagents; never wrapped or automated by kaneki on a personal plan.
Out of scope — Gemini CLI, pi, OpenCode, Cursor: presets may stay in code but are not planned, documented or tested here.

cards.title: Why it is agent-agnostic
items: Harness — one playbook + hosts/<h>/preamble.md + tiers.json (PR #22): any agent drives the same sdlc commands.
UI — ACP and the terminal: Zed doesn't care which agent runs.
State — ticket files on disk: each record keeps host + model; the next agent resumes from them.
View — the board reads the kernel and the session logs, never an agent.

cards.title: Planned work (see zed-workspace/plan.md)
items: P0 spike — Claude Agent loads skills/hooks over ACP; codex-acp and agy acp on Windows; zed://agent?prompt= behaviour.
P1 host fixes — SDLC_HOST in each rendered skill; .agents/ conflict; host-switch event; Antigravity refused by dispatch/runner; install --host required.
P2 board — node inspector, transcripts (Claude, Codex), in-flight, Open/Continue in Zed. P3 sdlc decide. P4 cost and budgets. P5 runner. P6 reflect node.
